description: 96.2% of household water from the coastal aquifer is non-potable. Earlier assessments put it at 90-95% unfit due to nitrogen and chloride; the World Bank reported only 5-10% of the aquifer yields drinkable water.
energy_note: Ninety-six per cent of the tap water, undrinkable.

description: The aquifer was being over-abstracted by 100 million cubic metres a year - almost double the safe rate - because desalination plants were not built, causing falling groundwater and seawater intrusion.
energy_note: Pumped at twice the rate it refills.

aspect: So drinking water is a purchased commodity
description: Households buy from private tankers and vendors of uncertain quality - a recurring cash cost, in one of the poorest places, for something that comes out of a tap elsewhere.
money_note: Annual household spend on drinking water.

aspect: Only a quarter of households had daily running water even before
description: Only a quarter of households received running water every day, and then for several hours only. The rest live on a rota and store what they can.
energy_note: Water arrives on a timetable, if at all.

aspect: Which makes the household water manager's day
description: Filling, storing, rationing, boiling, allocating between drinking, cooking, washing and laundry - a daily logistics job that falls almost entirely on women and is counted as leisure in every time-use survey.
time_note: Cumulative days per year on water logistics.
energy_note: Two hours a day, on water, uncounted.

aspect: And 90 million litres of sewage went into the sea daily
description: Untreated and partially treated sewage discharged off the coast at that rate creates a public health hazard that returns through the groundwater and the fish.
energy_note: It goes into the sea and comes back in the water.

energy_note: Pumped at twice the safe rate, until it turned to seawater.
